Decision: The Zombie module uses *Axis & Allies & Zombies* as its mechanical baseline, adapting it only where Global 1940's scale, existing systems, or map require it.
The Zombie module can function as an optional standalone module and can interact with the R&D system when both are enabled.
Global 1940 uses an adapted Zombie deck rather than directly porting the 1942 AAZ deck.

Principle: Preserve the AAZ loop, expand the event variety
Decision: The Global deck should retain the core AAZ mechanics while providing greater variety appropriate to the larger/longer Global game.
Randomness should primarily come from card draws and game-state-driven effects rather than arbitrary random territory selection.
Zombie events should preferentially interact with meaningful conditions on the actual Global map, such as units, factories, capitals, or recent combat.
Existing R&D technologies may provide additional contextual benefits when the Zombie module is active.
Dedicated Zombie technologies should remain limited and complementary to the main R&D tree rather than becoming a parallel military technology system.
Zombie events, Desperate Measures, existing R&D technologies, and dedicated Zombie research should be capable of interacting, while their precise relationships are determined separately.
The relationship between Desperate Measures and R&D is deliberately unresolved pending examination of the original AAZ cards.
